name: Fernando Castañeda

papers.title: EgoScale: Scaling Dexterous Manipulation with Diverse Egocentric Human Data
papers.abstract: Human behavior is among the most scalable sources of data for learning physical intelligence, yet how to effectively leverage it for dexterous manipulation remains unclear. While prior work demonstrates human-to-robot transfer in constrained settings, it is unclear whether large-scale human data can support fine-grained, high-degree-of-freedom dexterous manipulation. We present EgoScale, a human-to-dexterous-manipulation transfer framework built on large-scale egocentric human data. We train a Vision–Language–Action (VLA) model on over 20,854 hours of action-labeled egocentric human video—more than 20× larger than prior efforts—and uncover a log-linear scaling law between human data scale and validation loss. This validation loss strongly correlates with downstream real-robot performance, establishing large-scale human data as a predictable supervision source. Beyond scale, we introduce a simple two-stage transfer recipe: large-scale human pretraining followed by lightweight aligned human–robot mid-training. This enables strong long-horizon dexterous manipulation and one-shot task adaptation with minimal robot supervision. Our final policy improves the average success rate by 54% over a no-pretraining baseline using a 22-DoF dexterous robotic hand, and transfers effectively to robots with lower-DoF hands, indicating that large-scale human motion provides a reusable, embodiment-agnostic motor prior.
papers.summary: 用大规模第一人称人类操作视频预训练灵巧操作 VLA，再以轻量的人机对齐数据完成迁移。关注人类数据规模与真机表现的联系，以及低机器人数据条件下的长时任务和新手型适应。

papers.title: CHIP: Adaptive Compliance for Humanoid Control through Hindsight Perturbation
papers.abstract: Despite impressive agility in locomotion, humanoid forceful manipulation remains limited by the lack of scalable, easy to train compliant force control in reinforcement learning (RL). We introduce CHIP (\underline{C}ompliant \underline{H}umanoid natural control through h\underline{I}ndsight \underline{P}erturbation), a plug-and-play framework that bridges this gap. Our core insight is that a demonstrated motion can be reinterpreted, in hindsight, as a compliant response to an external perturbation. By adjusting only sparse motion goals in response to perturbations while leaving the dense reference trajectories untouched, CHIP allows compliant interaction behaviors to emerge naturally without degrading motion tracking rewards. A single CHIP policy successfully executes forceful interaction tasks (e.g., wiping, cart pushing, door opening) alongside highly agile behaviors (e.g., dancing, running), and seamlessly extends to multi-agent cooperative transport.
